sourceMetadata.title: How to INSTANTLY Relieve Gluteus Medius Pain
sourceMetadata.description:
Dr. Rowe demonstrates simple exercises to quickly relieve tightness and pain in the gluteus medius muscle.

The gluteus medius is a fan-shaped muscle located in the buttock. It stretches from the back of the pelvis to the outer thigh and hip area.

When this muscle becomes strained or inflamed, it can cause pain in the lower back, buttocks, and especially the outer hip and thigh. A common symptom is discomfort along the outer (lateral) side of the hip and thigh.

This pain often stems from a combination of muscle weakness and tightness, which leads to strain and inflammation.

To relieve this, we’ll focus on both lengthening and strengthening the glutes—providing quick relief and long-term results.

Each exercise targets the gluteus medius in a unique way. For best results, try them all and stick with the ones that bring you the most relief.

Let us know which one works best for you!

sourceMetadata.title: The Sciatica Muscle (How to Release It for INSTANT RELIEF)
sourceMetadata.description:
Dr. Rowe goes over how to release the sciatica muscle.

If you're unfamiliar with the piriformis, it's a muscle that lies underneath the glutes and near the sciatic nerve.

When it becomes strained and inflamed, it can irritate the nearby sciatic nerve, causing sciatica symptoms (pain, numbness and tingling) down the leg. This is commonly known as piriformis syndrome.

What usually causes this is a blend of tightness and weakness in the glutes and piriformis muscles. 

To make getting relief easy, this video will focus on lengthening and strengthening these muscles for both quick and long lasting sciatica relief.

Watch now and get instant piriformis and sciatica pain relief!

If you're unfamiliar with BPPV, it's a type of vertigo that is commonly seen with quick motions of the head (think turning your head, or rolling over in bed). A common cause of this is displaced crystals in your inner ear canal that disrupt near-by balance receptors.

sourceMetadata.title: How to Relieve TMJ Pain at Home | 30 SECOND RELIEF
sourceMetadata.description:
Dr. Rowe shows how to get quick TMJ pain relief at home, using NO EQUIPMENT.

Dr. Rowe shows how to quickly relieve iliotibial band syndrome pain.

The iliotibial band, also known as the IT band, is a hot spot for outer knee, leg, and hip pain.

sourceMetadata.title: How to Make Your Shoulder Blades NOT Stick Out
sourceMetadata.description:
In this video,  Dr. Rowe shows how to make your shoulder blades not stick out. 

So we’re going to help tackle scapular dyskinesis or SICK scapula, which is a malposition of the shoulder blades that also affects its function and movement. 

Common symptoms of this include anterior shoulder pain, pain around the shoulder blades and upper back, a low shoulder, and winged scapula (which can be very unsightly).

These exercises are going to target a main instigator of scapular winging and dyskinesis, which is the serratus anterior muscle. 

Why this muscle is so important is because it functions to pull the scapula forward around the chest. Another big role of the serratus anterior is to help keep the scapula flush against the rib cage and aid in shoulder stability.

As you can see, any issues with this muscle can definitely lead to future problems with the shoulder blades. 

So if you are having issues with scapular dyskinesis or winging of scapula, these exercises might be a good place to start and see if it can be improved by targeting the serratus anterior muscle. 

These exercises are straightforward and easy to do. They'll be shown in a three step progression, so make sure to try them all to get the most out of it.

sourceMetadata.title: How to POP Your Hip Back in Place
sourceMetadata.description:
So does your hip feel out of place and it’s causing pain, discomfort, or other issues? 

In this video, Dr. Rowe shows some easy ways to pop your hip back in place for INSTANT RELIEF.

Included are two exercises that will fix a hip that is out of alignment. They’re really easy to do, don’t require any special equipment, and can be done in the comfort of your own home.

Why these exercises are so effective is due to helping reset the ‘ball and socket’ joint of the hip. It’s a type of joint in which a ball-shaped surface of one rounded bone fits into a cup-like depression of another bone. 

This allows for a lot of movement in many directions, but also requires a strong support system of soft tissues like cartilage, muscles, and tendons.

That’s why a lot of hip pain comes from soft tissue injuries.

Here’s a key point: your hip range of motion depends on the proper movement of the ball and socket joint. If the soft tissue is strained, it can cause tightness and less range of motion. 

Also, the smooth glide of the hips can be impacted, leading to a pop or crack sensation when you try to move it from a locked-up position. 

So again, think of these exercises as resetting the hip joint, helping to release tension on the soft tissues supporting the hips, and re-positioning the ball onto the socket. 

This should help you have more overall movement in the hips, less tightness and dull, achy pain, and less of those pop and crack sounds.

WHAT IS CERVICAL RADICULOPATHY?

👉 Cervical radiculopathy is caused when a spinal nerve root in the neck becomes pinched or irritated. It’s usually caused by a herniated disc or spinal stenosis. 

These nerve roots are responsible for supplying sensation and muscle function to the upper part of the body.

Irritation to these nerve roots may cause pain, numbness, and weakness to the area where the nerves travel. 

👉 Symptoms usually are sharp, shooting pains in the neck, shoulder, arm, or hand.

sourceMetadata.title: What is Spondylolisthesis? SpineCare Chiropractic in St. Joseph MI
sourceMetadata.description:
https://www.bestspinecare.com

SPONDYLOLISTHESIS EXPLAINED.

Spondylolisthesis sounds like a long, fancy word. But if you break it down, ‘spondy’ means spine and ‘listhesis’ means slip. So put together, spondylolisthesis means ‘slip of the spine.’

This is where one vertebrae is shifting forward (or backwards) relative to the vertebrae above or below it. 

It’s most commonly seen at the lowest lumbar segment, L5, and the first sacral segment, S1. 

The big issue with spondylolisthesis is abnormal movement in the spine, which leads to instability. So the back or neck becomes unstable, making it more prone to injury. 

It can be caused by a birth defect, degenerative disc disease, or traumatic injury. 

Symptoms include joint and muscle pain in the area affected, and it’s possible to have spinal nerve impingement (due to the shift) leading to traveling pains, numbness, and weakness.

DEGENERATIVE DISC DISEASE EXERCISES.⠀
⠀
Degenerative disc disease (DDD), also known as spondylosis, is a common result of the aging process.

THE BIRD DOG:⠀
1️⃣ Start on all fours.⠀
2️⃣ Make sure arms inline with shoulders, knees are straight under the hips, back is straight.⠀
3️⃣ Slowly, raise one leg so it's in line with the back. ⠀
4️⃣ Return to starting position, then repeat on other side.⠀

DEGENERATIVE DISC DISEASE PAIN RELIEF.

Degenerative disc disease (DDD), also known as spondylosis, is a common result of the aging process. 

Not every case of DDD  will cause debilitating pain, but the process may cause certain affects that will impact daily life, including less flexibility due to joint stiffness.

👉 These stretches are geared towards helping relieve some of the painful symptoms caused by DDD. 

👉 They may help improve lost flexibility (and muscle strength) and aid in better support of the spine.

SINGLE KNEE TO THE CHEST:
1️⃣ Lie flat on back.
2️⃣ Bring one leg towards chest, while the other leg remains straight as possible.
3️⃣ Hold for 15-30 seconds.
4️⃣ Relax and repeat 3-5 times. 

DOUBLE KNEE TO THE CHEST:
1️⃣ Lie flat on back.
2️⃣ Bring both legs towards chest.
3️⃣ Hold for 15-30 seconds.
4️⃣ Relax and repeat 3-5 times. 

LUMBAR ROTATION:
1️⃣ Lie flat on bacl.
2️⃣ Bend knees, keep feet flat.
3️⃣ Slowly, bend towards one side until a good stretch is felt.
4️⃣ Hold 2-3 seconds, return to starting position, and repeat on other side.
5️⃣ Do 10-15 complete cycles.
NOTE: keep the hips/bottom flat as possible! Only rotate the legs, don't twist the torso.

sourceMetadata.title: What is Degenerative Disc Disease? DDD Explained by St. Joseph, MI Chiropractor
sourceMetadata.description:
https://www.bestspinecare.com

WHAT IS DEGENERATIVE DISC DISEASE? ⠀⠀
⠀
Here's a no-nonsense explanation of one of the most common causes of pain in the neck and low back. No doctor-speak that leaves more questions than answers. 😕⠀⠀
⠀
Degenerative Disc Disease is a normal process of aging, but can also be from repetitive stress and injury on the spine. Think wear and tear on the spinal discs.⠀⠀
⠀
The spinal discs are soft, shock absorbing cushions ↕️ of the spine that fit between the vertebrae, the blocks that make up the spine.⠀⠀
⠀
During the aging process, the discs start to lose water content 💧 and become less flexible. With the disc weakening over time, they can start to bulge and pinch onto nearby nerves, causing shooting pains. 
⠀
As degeneration progresses, the disc may also begin to thin, which lessens the shock-absorbing effect of the disc. This thinning puts more stress on the vertebrae, which will lead to the formation of bone spurs, called osteophytes. ⠀⠀
⠀
If it gets severe enough, the bone spurs may grow large enough to make contact with a nerve or the spinal cord. This is where a pinched nerve comes in, causing sharp and shooting pains. ⚡⚡⠀⠀
⠀
Also, numbness, tingling, and muscle weakness can be experienced over the affected area. 
⠀⠀
Hope this helps explain it in a more understandable way!

sourceMetadata.title: How to Test for Piriformis Syndrome | St. Joseph, MI Chiropractor
sourceMetadata.description:

Piriformis syndrome is commonly mistaken for herniated disc in the low back, since they have a lot of similar pain patterns. 
.
➡️ What’s different about pirifomis syndrome, though, is that it’s a muscle issue (and not a spinal joint problem). 
.
It occurs when the piriformis muscle (which lies deep to the glute or buttock) spasms and irritates the sciatic nerve. ⚡️⚡️
.
Symptoms usually include tenderness and pain in the buttock area, and possible sciatica like shooting pains, numbness, and weakness in the leg.  
.
➡️ Long periods of sitting or driving tend to be a main trigger for piriformis issues. Strenuous exercise and unresolved sacroiliac joint, hip, or spinal injuries can also put strain on this muscle. 
.
So if there's a lot of pain while walking up stairs, sitting, or running… there’s a chance it could be a piriformis issue. 
.
